## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

The legacy fetcher must follow the existing retry cap before merge because prolonged outages can tie up worker threads.

## Changes

The pull request adds a legacy inventory fetcher with eight attempts and a health probe with three. It adds shared tests for success, retry exhaustion, and immediate HTTP errors, and proposes exempting legacy modules from the retry cap.

## Critical

- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy inventory requests at three attempts — When the inventory endpoint keeps timing out, the fetcher makes eight attempts. `docs/review-rules.md:5` requires “Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts.” — When each attempt reaches the 10-second timeout, the five extra attempts and delays keep the caller waiting another 55 seconds. — Fix: Update the legacy case in `tests/test_retries.py` to expect three attempts.

## Suggestions

- app/health.py:21 — tests — Test retries after a response body times out — The shared tests would pass if either helper stopped retrying when `resp.read()` raises `TimeoutError` after the response opens. The retry fixture raises only from `urlopen`. — A stalled response body can lose retry protection in either helper without a test failure. — Fix: Extend `test_returns_body` with a response whose `read()` times out before a later attempt succeeds.
